I'd convinced myself our app was unique, and it was only after launch that I discovered there were at least thirty others doing almost exactly the same thing, several of them backed by far bigger budgets than ours. We had spent eighteen months perfecting features that, it turned out, everyone else already offered. We never stood a chance of being noticed. When we shut down, I went quiet about it for a long time. At networking events I'd mumble something vague about 'pivoting' and change the subject; it took me nearly two years before I could describe what had happened without feeling my face go red. These days I talk about it quite freely – I've even given a couple of talks on the subject – and I wish I'd got there sooner. Looking back, the experience taught me more than any business course could have.

sections.heading: Isabel Moreno – a fashion label
sections.text: On paper, the brand was doing fine. Orders were growing, the bank was patient, and a couple of boutiques wanted to stock the collection. The real problem was me. I insisted on doing everything myself – design, sourcing, the website, even packing the parcels – because I couldn't bear the thought of anyone else getting it wrong. By the second year I was working eighteen-hour days and was utterly exhausted. My business partner, who was also one of my oldest friends, tried repeatedly to take some of the load off, and I kept pushing her away. Eventually she walked out, and we didn't speak for nearly three years. If I had brought in an experienced mentor, or even just hired a part-time assistant, at the start rather than when it was already too late, I think things could have turned out very differently.

sections.heading: Raj Patel – an online tutoring platform
sections.text: I still believe in the idea. An online platform connecting students with tutors, with proper vetting and fair pay – there was nothing wrong with that. The problem was that we launched in 2011, when most families were still wary of paying for anything educational that happened through a screen, and broadband in many homes was patchy at best. Ten years later, platforms almost identical to ours were thriving. It was a painful lesson in how much depends on circumstances you can't control. What I took away from it, more than anything, was a different attitude to the people who work for me. In that first company I treated staff as an extension of my own ambition and expected them to share my obsession. Now, running my second business, I'm much more conscious that people have lives outside work, and I think my team is happier and more productive as a result.

questions.statement: failed to research how many similar products already existed

why.en: B 'barely looked at what else was out there' and only discovered 'at least thirty others' after launch. D mentions similar platforms, but they appeared ten years later.
why.bg: B 'barely looked at what else was out there' и чак след старта открива 'at least thirty others'. D споменава подобни платформи, но те се появяват десет години по-късно.

questions.statement: went ahead despite warnings from several people

why.en: A: 'Everyone told me the location was wrong … I listened politely and signed the lease anyway.'
why.bg: A: 'Everyone told me the location was wrong … I listened politely and signed the lease anyway.' – продължава въпреки предупрежденията.

questions.statement: lost a close friendship as a result of the business

why.en: C's partner, 'one of my oldest friends', walked out and they 'didn't speak for nearly three years'.
why.bg: Съдружничката на C, 'one of my oldest friends', си тръгва и двете 'didn't speak for nearly three years'.

questions.statement: believes the business was launched too early

why.en: D launched when families were 'still wary' and broadband was 'patchy'; 'ten years later' identical platforms thrived – the timing was wrong, not the idea.
why.bg: D стартира, когато семействата са 'still wary', а интернетът – 'patchy'; 'ten years later' почти същите платформи процъфтяват – проблемът е моментът, не идеята.

questions.statement: remembers feeling relieved when the business finally closed

why.en: A felt 'a kind of lightness, as if I'd been holding my breath for a year and could finally exhale'. B's feelings on closing were embarrassment, not relief.
why.bg: A усеща 'a kind of lightness, as if I'd been holding my breath for a year and could finally exhale'. B след затварянето изпитва срам, не облекчение.

questions.statement: regrets not getting outside support earlier

why.en: C wishes she had brought in a mentor or assistant 'at the start rather than when it was already too late'. B is the trap: his 'I wish I'd got there sooner' is about talking openly, not about getting help.
why.bg: C съжалява, че не е взела ментор или асистент 'at the start rather than when it was already too late'. Капанът е B: неговото 'I wish I'd got there sooner' е за откритото говорене, не за търсене на помощ.

questions.statement: says the experience changed the way they treat staff

why.en: D now realises 'people have lives outside work' instead of treating staff 'as an extension of my own ambition'.
why.bg: D вече осъзнава, че 'people have lives outside work', вместо да гледа на служителите 'as an extension of my own ambition'.

questions.statement: was initially too embarrassed to discuss what had happened

why.en: B would 'mumble something vague' and change the subject, and needed 'nearly two years' to talk about it without blushing. A also kept quiet, but before the closure, not about it afterwards.
why.bg: B 'mumble something vague' и сменя темата, трябват му 'nearly two years', за да говори без да се изчерви. A също мълчи, но преди затварянето, а не след това.

questions.statement: insists that the business was not failing financially

why.en: C: 'On paper, the brand was doing fine. Orders were growing, the bank was patient… The real problem was me.' D defends his idea, but says nothing about the finances being healthy.
why.bg: C: 'On paper, the brand was doing fine. Orders were growing, the bank was patient… The real problem was me.' D защитава идеята си, но не казва, че финансите са били наред.

questions.statement: describes the exact moment they realised the business would not survive

why.en: A recalls 'a wet Tuesday in February' when she served eleven customers and knew 'with total clarity, that it was over'.
why.bg: A си спомня 'a wet Tuesday in February', когато обслужва единайсет клиенти и разбира 'with total clarity, that it was over'.

tasks.title: Concrete feelings
tasks.instructions: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
tasks.text:
Few architectural styles {{1}} opinion as sharply as Brutalism. To its detractors, the raw concrete blocks that sprang up across Europe in the decades after the Second World War are nothing short of an eyesore, a {{2}} reminder of failed social experiments. Yet in recent years the style has enjoyed an unlikely {{3}} in popularity, particularly among young people who first encountered it through photographs shared online.

Admirers argue that critics have {{4}} the point. Brutalist buildings, they say, were born of a genuine commitment to providing decent housing and public amenities for all, {{5}} of income, and their honesty about materials is refreshing in an age of glossy facades. Whether this enthusiasm will translate into protection for the buildings themselves remains to be seen. Many are in a poor state of {{6}}, and the cost of restoring them often far {{7}} that of knocking them down. For campaigners, time is fast {{8}} out.

why.en: 'Divide opinion' means people strongly disagree about something. 'Separate' has a similar basic meaning but does not collocate with 'opinion'.
why.bg: 'Divide opinion' значи, че хората силно не са съгласни помежду си. 'Separate' има сходно основно значение, но не се съчетава с 'opinion'.

why.en: 'A stark reminder' = a very clear, unpleasant reminder. 'Sheer' intensifies nouns like 'luck' or 'size', and 'bare' means 'minimum' (the bare essentials), so neither fits.
why.bg: 'A stark reminder' = ясно и неприятно напомняне. 'Sheer' усилва думи като 'luck' или 'size', а 'bare' значи 'минимален' (the bare essentials), така че не пасват.

why.en: 'A surge in popularity' is the natural collocation for a sudden rise. 'Rush' suggests many people moving or buying quickly (a rush for tickets), not a rise in a level.
why.bg: 'A surge in popularity' е естествената колокация за рязко покачване. 'Rush' предполага много хора, които бързат за нещо (a rush for tickets), а не ръст на ниво.

why.en: 'Miss the point' = fail to understand what matters. 'Lost' is tempting because of 'lose the plot', but 'lose the point' is not the idiom.
why.bg: 'Miss the point' = не схващам същността. 'Lost' изкушава заради 'lose the plot', но 'lose the point' не е идиом.

why.en: Only 'regardless' is followed by 'of' to mean 'without considering'. 'Despite' and 'notwithstanding' are prepositions themselves and are never followed by 'of'; 'apart from' needs 'from'.
why.bg: Само 'regardless' върви с 'of' в значение 'независимо от'. 'Despite' и 'notwithstanding' сами са предлози и никога не се следват от 'of'; 'apart' иска 'from'.

why.en: The fixed phrase is 'in a poor/good state of repair'. 'Condition' is close in meaning, but we say 'in poor condition', not 'a poor state of condition'.
why.bg: Устойчивият израз е 'in a poor/good state of repair'. 'Condition' е близко по смисъл, но казваме 'in poor condition', а не 'a poor state of condition'.

why.en: 'Exceed' = be greater than (an amount). 'Overtakes' is tempting because it suggests going past, but it describes a process of catching up, not a fixed comparison of costs; 'overcome' and 'surmount' are used for problems.
why.bg: 'Exceed' = надвишавам (количество). 'Overtakes' изкушава, защото значи 'изпреварвам', но описва процес на настигане, а не просто сравнение на суми; 'overcome' и 'surmount' се използват за проблеми.

why.en: 'Time is running out' = there is little time left. 'Wearing out' exists but means becoming damaged through use, and 'time is passing' does not combine with 'out'.
why.bg: 'Time is running out' = времето изтича. 'Wearing out' съществува, но значи 'износва се', а 'time is passing' не се съчетава с 'out'.

tasks.title: The shorter week
tasks.instructions: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
tasks.text:
When a handful of companies first experimented with a four-day working week, many observers {{1}} the idea off as a publicity stunt. Several years and numerous trials later, the concept is gaining {{2}}. In most pilot schemes, productivity held {{3}} or even rose, while staff reported lower levels of stress and burnout.

Sceptics, however, point out that the firms taking part were self-selected and therefore hardly {{4}} of the economy as a whole. A software start-up may be able to compress its working hours with little difficulty; a hospital or a care home, by {{5}}, cannot simply close on Fridays. There is also the question of whether the gains will {{6}} the test of time once the novelty has worn off. Advocates dismiss these concerns as mere teething {{7}}, but even they concede that the model is unlikely to be a one-size-fits-all solution. For now, the jury is still {{8}}.

why.en: 'Write something off as' = decide it is a failure or not worth attention. 'Put off' exists but means 'postpone' or 'discourage', and cannot take 'as'.
why.bg: 'Write something off as' = отписвам нещо като провал или несериозно. 'Put off' съществува, но значи 'отлагам' или 'отказвам някого', и не върви с 'as'.

why.en: An idea 'gains traction' when it becomes accepted. 'Grip' and 'hold' are tempting because of 'get a grip' and 'take hold', but neither combines with 'gain' in this sense.
why.bg: Една идея 'gains traction', когато започва да се приема. 'Grip' и 'hold' изкушават заради 'get a grip' и 'take hold', но не се съчетават с 'gain' в този смисъл.

why.en: 'Hold steady' = stay at the same level. 'Flat' is tempting because we say figures 'remained flat', but it does not combine with 'hold'.
why.bg: 'Hold steady' = остава на същото ниво. 'Flat' изкушава, защото казваме, че цифрите 'remained flat', но не се съчетава с 'hold'.

why.en: 'Representative of' = a fair sample of. 'Symbolic of' means 'standing for an idea', which is not the point: the firms are not typical, not symbols.
why.bg: 'Representative of' = представителна извадка за. 'Symbolic of' значи 'символ на нещо', а тук въпросът е, че фирмите не са типични, а не че са символ.

why.en: 'By contrast' is the fixed linking phrase. 'Distinction' and 'difference' are close in meaning but do not form a phrase with 'by'.
why.bg: 'By contrast' е устойчивият свързващ израз – за разлика от това. 'Distinction' и 'difference' са близки по смисъл, но не образуват израз с 'by'.

why.en: 'Stand the test of time' = remain valid or popular for a long time. 'Pass' is the tempting option because we 'pass a test', but it is not used in this idiom.
why.bg: 'Stand the test of time' = издържам проверката на времето. 'Pass' изкушава, защото казваме 'pass a test', но в този идиом не се използва.

why.en: 'Teething troubles' (or 'problems') are small problems at the start of a project. 'Pains' is the trap: it belongs to a different phrase, 'growing pains'.
why.bg: 'Teething troubles' (или 'problems') са дребни начални проблеми. Капанът е 'pains': той е от друг израз – 'growing pains'.

why.en: 'The jury is still out' = no decision has been reached yet. 'Absent' has a related literal meaning but is not part of the idiom.
why.bg: 'The jury is still out' = все още няма окончателна присъда/решение. 'Absent' има близко буквално значение, но не е част от идиома.

tasks.title: Tunes that won't leave
tasks.instructions: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.
tasks.text:
Almost everyone has experienced an earworm – a fragment of music that loops endlessly in the mind, often {{9}} the listener's will. Surveys suggest that more than ninety per cent of people are affected at least once a week, and for a minority the experience is {{10}} persistent that it interferes with concentration.

Why certain tunes get stuck while others fade away {{11}} trace is a question that has intrigued psychologists for years. The songs most likely to linger, it seems, share a number of features: a fast tempo, a simple melodic shape and, crucially, some unexpected twist {{12}} sets them apart from more predictable tunes. Recent exposure also plays a part; {{13}} more often we hear a song, the greater the chance that it will return unbidden.

As for getting rid of an earworm, the advice is somewhat counterintuitive. Trying hard not to think about the tune rarely works and may {{14}} make matters worse. {{15}} than fighting it, researchers suggest, we should engage with it – for example, by listening to the song all the way through. Chewing gum, oddly {{16}}, has also been found to help.

why.en: 'Against somebody's will' = without their agreement. It's a fixed phrase; 'despite' is close in meaning but 'despite the listener's will' isn't idiomatic.
why.bg: 'Against somebody's will' = против волята на някого. Устойчив израз е; 'despite' е близко по смисъл, но 'despite the listener's will' не е естествено.

why.en: 'So + adjective + that' expresses result. 'Such' would need a noun (such a persistent experience that…).
why.bg: 'So + прилагателно + that' изразява резултат ('толкова…, че'). 'Such' иска съществително (such a persistent experience that…).

why.en: 'Without (a) trace' = completely, leaving nothing behind. 'Fade away without trace' is a set combination.
why.bg: 'Without (a) trace' = безследно. 'Fade away without trace' е устойчиво съчетание.

why.en: A relative pronoun is needed as the subject of 'sets': 'some unexpected twist that sets them apart'. 'What' can't follow a noun.
why.bg: Нужно е относително местоимение като подлог на 'sets': 'some unexpected twist that sets them apart'. 'What' не може да стои след съществително.

why.en: 'The more often …, the greater …' – both halves of the double comparative need 'the'. The second 'the greater' is a clear signal.
why.bg: 'The more often …, the greater …' – двете части на двойното сравнение изискват 'the'. Второто 'the greater' е ясният сигнал.

why.en: 'May even make matters worse' – 'even' adds emphasis to a surprising, stronger point. 'Also' is possible grammatically but doesn't express the idea of going further.
why.bg: 'May even make matters worse' – 'even' подсилва изненадващо, по-силно твърдение ('дори'). 'Also' е граматически възможно, но не носи идеята за 'отиване по-далеч'.

why.en: 'Rather than fighting it, … we should engage with it' – 'rather than + -ing' = instead of. The 'than' after the gap makes 'instead' impossible.
why.bg: 'Rather than fighting it, … we should engage with it' – 'rather than + -ing' = вместо да. 'Than' след празното място изключва 'instead'.

why.en: 'Oddly enough' (like 'strangely enough', 'funnily enough') comments on something surprising. It's a fixed pattern of adverb + 'enough'.
why.bg: 'Oddly enough' (като 'strangely enough', 'funnily enough') = колкото и да е странно. Това е устойчив модел наречие + 'enough'.

tasks.title: Bringing back the mammoth
tasks.instructions: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.
tasks.text:
Thanks to advances in genetic engineering, the prospect of bringing extinct species back to life is no {{9}} confined to the realm of science fiction. Several research teams are currently working on projects to recreate animals such as the woolly mammoth, {{10}} last populations died out around four thousand years ago.

Supporters of 'de-extinction' argue that humanity has a moral duty to undo some of the damage it has caused. {{11}} it not for human hunting and habitat destruction, they point out, many of these creatures would still be alive today. Restoring them could also benefit entire ecosystems: mammoths, {{12}} instance, may once have helped to maintain open grasslands.

Opponents, however, warn that the money would be better spent protecting the species we already have. There is also the risk that the mere possibility of reviving lost animals could encourage complacency: if extinction is no longer forever, why go to such lengths to prevent {{13}}? And even if the technology succeeds, there is no guarantee that a resurrected species could survive in a world that has changed {{14}} recognition since it vanished. {{15}} exciting the prospect may be, then, it may be wise to proceed with caution – and to remember that prevention is, {{16}} usual, far cheaper than cure.

why.en: 'No longer' = not any more. 'No more' is used with nouns or as a comparative of quantity, not as a time adverb before a participle like 'confined'.
why.bg: 'No longer' = вече не. 'No more' се използва със съществителни или за количество, а не като наречие за време пред причастие като 'confined'.

why.en: 'Whose' shows possession: the mammoth's last populations. 'Which' would need a different structure (the last populations of which…).
why.bg: 'Whose' изразява притежание: последните популации на мамута. 'Which' би изисквало друга конструкция (the last populations of which…).

why.en: 'Were it not for' = if it were not for – an inverted conditional without 'if'. 'Had' is wrong here because it needs 'been' (Had it not been for).
why.bg: 'Were it not for' = ако не беше – условно изречение с инверсия, без 'if'. 'Had' е грешно тук, защото иска 'been' (Had it not been for).

why.en: 'For instance' = for example. Only 'for' forms this phrase.
why.bg: 'For instance' = например. Само 'for' образува този израз.

why.en: 'Prevent' needs an object, and the pronoun refers back to 'extinction'. 'This' is possible in theory but sounds unnatural; 'it' is the expected answer.
why.bg: 'Prevent' изисква допълнение, а местоимението се отнася към 'extinction'. 'This' теоретично е възможно, но звучи неестествено; очакваният отговор е 'it'.

why.en: 'Change beyond recognition' = change so much that it can't be recognised. 'Out of recognition' would need two words; 'past recognition' is rarer but acceptable.
why.bg: 'Change beyond recognition' = променям се до неузнаваемост. 'Out of recognition' са две думи; 'past recognition' е по-рядко, но е приемливо.

why.en: 'However + adjective + subject + may be' = no matter how. 'Although' can't be followed directly by an adjective in this way.
why.bg: 'However + прилагателно + подлог + may be' = колкото и да е. 'Although' не може да е последвано директно от прилагателно по този начин.

why.en: 'As usual' = as is normally the case. 'Like usual' is informal and not accepted in the exam.
why.bg: 'As usual' = както обикновено. 'Like usual' е разговорно и не се приема на изпита.

tasks.title: What maps don't show
tasks.instructions: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals to form a word that fits in the gap.
tasks.text:
Maps are often regarded as {{17}} (OBJECT) representations of the world, but historians of cartography have long argued otherwise. Every map, they point out, reflects a series of choices about what to include, what to leave out and what to place at the centre – choices that are rarely {{18}} (POLITICS) neutral.

Consider the familiar world map found in so many classrooms. Its projection, devised in the sixteenth century as an aid to {{19}} (NAVIGATE), greatly exaggerates the size of regions far from the equator. Greenland appears roughly the same size as Africa, despite being some fourteen times smaller. Critics argue that such {{20}} (TORT) have subtly shaped perceptions of the relative importance of different parts of the globe.

Alternative projections exist, of course, but each involves its own {{21}} (TRADE): preserving accurate areas, for instance, inevitably distorts shapes. It is a mathematical {{22}} (POSSIBLE) to flatten a sphere without some loss of accuracy. The real problem, then, is not that maps are imperfect, but that users are often {{23}} (OBLIVION) to their limitations. Teaching children to read maps {{24}} (CRITIC) may be as important as teaching them to read maps at all.

why.en: An adjective before 'representations', meaning neutral and factual: object → objective.
why.bg: Прилагателно пред 'representations' със значение 'неутрален, обективен': object → objective.

why.en: An adverb modifying the adjective 'neutral': politics → political → politically.
why.bg: Наречие към прилагателното 'neutral': politics → political → politically.

why.en: After 'an aid to' we need a noun: navigate → navigation. 'Navigating' is possible after 'to' only in other structures; the noun is expected here.
why.bg: След 'an aid to' трябва съществително: navigate → navigation. Тук се очаква съществителното, а не -ing формата.

why.en: Prefix + suffix + plural: dis- + tort + -ion + -s. 'Such' and the plural verb 'have' show a plural noun is needed – 'distortion' loses a mark.
why.bg: Представка + наставка + множествено число: dis- + tort + -ion + -s. 'Such' и глаголът 'have' показват, че трябва множествено число – 'distortion' губи точката.

why.en: A compound noun: trade-off = a balance between two things you can't have at the same time, which matches the example that follows.
why.bg: Сложно съществително: trade-off = компромис между две неща, които не можеш да имаш едновременно – точно като примера след двоеточието.

why.en: After 'a mathematical' we need a noun, and the meaning is negative: im- + possible + -ity → impossibility. 'Possibility' would contradict 'without some loss of accuracy'.
why.bg: След 'a mathematical' трябва съществително, а смисълът е отрицателен: im- + possible + -ity → impossibility. 'Possibility' би противоречало на смисъла.

why.en: 'Oblivious to' = completely unaware of. The adjective comes from 'oblivion' and takes 'to' (or 'of').
why.bg: 'Oblivious to' = напълно несъзнаващ. Прилагателното идва от 'oblivion' и върви с 'to' (или 'of').

why.en: An adverb describing how to read maps: critic → critical → critically (questioning what they show).
why.bg: Наречие, което описва как да четем картите: critic → critical → critically (критично, с въпроси).

tasks.title: Sharing with strangers
tasks.instructions: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals to form a word that fits in the gap.
tasks.text:
Not long ago, the idea of staying in a stranger's spare room or climbing into a stranger's car would have struck most people as {{17}} (THINK). Today, such arrangements are commonplace, thanks to digital platforms that connect people with spare resources to those who need them.

The {{18}} (ATTRACT) of this 'sharing economy' is easy to understand. For consumers, it offers convenience and choice at {{19}} (COMPETE) prices; for providers, a welcome source of extra income. Its {{20}} (SUPPORT) also claim environmental benefits, arguing that sharing makes more efficient use of goods that would otherwise lie idle.

The picture, however, is more complicated. In many cities, the conversion of homes into short-term rentals has been blamed for {{21}} (SKY) rents and a shortage of housing for local residents. Workers, meanwhile, often find themselves without the protections enjoyed by {{22}} (CONVENTION) employees, such as sick pay and paid holidays. Regulators have been {{23}} (NOTORIOUS) slow to respond, partly because the platforms operate across borders. Striking a balance between innovation and fairness will require considerable {{24}} (INGENIOUS) on the part of lawmakers.

why.en: Prefix and suffix: un- + think + -able = impossible to imagine. 'Thinkable' would contradict 'Not long ago…'.
why.bg: Представка и наставка: un- + think + -able = немислимо. 'Thinkable' противоречи на 'Not long ago…'.

why.en: A singular noun after 'The': attraction (or attractiveness) = what makes it appealing. 'Attractions' is wrong because of the singular verb 'is'.
why.bg: Съществително в единствено число след 'The': attraction (или attractiveness) = привлекателността. 'Attractions' е грешно заради глагола 'is'.

why.en: 'Competitive prices' = prices as low as or lower than others'. Note the internal change: compete → competitive (not 'competetive').
why.bg: 'Competitive prices' = конкурентни цени. Внимавай с вътрешната промяна: compete → competitive (не 'competetive').

why.en: A plural noun for people: the plural verb 'claim' shows it must be 'supporters', not 'supporter'.
why.bg: Съществително за хора в множествено число: глаголът 'claim' показва, че трябва 'supporters', а не 'supporter'.

why.en: A compound participle adjective before 'rents': sky + rocket + -ing = rising very fast.
why.bg: Сложно причастие пред 'rents': sky + rocket + -ing = рязко растящи.

why.en: An adjective before 'employees': convention → conventional (ordinary, traditional).
why.bg: Прилагателно пред 'employees': convention → conventional (обикновени, традиционни).

why.en: An adverb modifying 'slow': notorious → notoriously (well known for something bad).
why.bg: Наречие към 'slow': notorious → notoriously (печално известно).

why.en: The usual noun from 'ingenious' involves an internal change: ingenious → ingenuity. ('Ingeniousness' is rare but acceptable.) Don't confuse it with 'ingenuousness', which comes from 'ingenuous' (= naive).
why.bg: Обичайното съществително от 'ingenious' е с вътрешна промяна: ingenious → ingenuity (изобретателност). ('Ingeniousness' е рядко, но се приема.) Не бъркай с 'ingenuousness' – то идва от 'ingenuous' (= наивен).

tasks.title: Key word transformations: drill A
tasks.instructions: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

questions.first: You must not open this door under any circumstances.
accept: On no account must you open
On no account should you open

why.en: 'On no account' at the start triggers inversion: On no account + modal + subject + verb. 'On no account you must open' has no inversion and loses a mark.
why.bg: 'On no account' в началото изисква инверсия: On no account + модален глагол + подлог + глагол. 'On no account you must open' е без инверсия и губи точка.

questions.first: It's possible that the delay was caused by a technical fault.

why.en: Possibility in the past + passive: may + have been + past participle. 'May be caused' refers to the present.
why.bg: Възможност в миналото + страдателен залог: may + have been + минало причастие. 'May be caused' се отнася за настоящето.

questions.first: Jack has finally become accustomed to working night shifts.

why.en: 'Get used to + -ing' = become accustomed. The 'to' is a preposition, so it's followed by -ing: 'got used to work' loses a mark.
why.bg: 'Get used to + -ing' = свиквам с. 'To' тук е предлог, затова след него идва -ing: 'got used to work' губи точка.

questions.first: Most people were unaware of how serious the problem was.

why.en: 'The (full) extent of the problem' = how big or serious it is. 'Unaware' needs 'of' first, and 'extent' needs 'of' after it.
why.bg: 'The (full) extent of the problem' = истинският мащаб на проблема. 'Unaware' иска 'of', а 'extent' също е последвано от 'of'.

questions.first: My brother was the person who persuaded me to take up running.

why.en: 'Talk somebody into doing something' = persuade them. 'Into' is followed by -ing; 'talked me to take' is wrong.
why.bg: 'Talk somebody into doing something' = убеждавам някого да направи нещо. След 'into' идва -ing; 'talked me to take' е грешно.

questions.first: If it hadn't been for the rain, the match would have finished on time.
questions.before: The match would have finished on time

why.en: 'But for + noun' = if it hadn't been for – a formal conditional without 'if'. It's followed by a noun phrase, not a clause.
why.bg: 'But for + съществително' = ако не беше – официално условие без 'if'. Следва съществително, не цяло изречение.

tasks.title: Key word transformations: drill B
tasks.instructions: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

questions.first: As soon as the guests arrived, the power went off.
accept: sooner had the guests arrived than

why.en: 'No sooner had + subject + past participle + than' – inversion after 'No sooner', and 'than' (not 'when') introduces the second event.
why.bg: 'No sooner had + подлог + минало причастие + than' – инверсия след 'No sooner', а второто действие се въвежда с 'than' (не 'when').

questions.first: People say that the castle was built in the eleventh century.
accept: is said to have been built

why.en: Personal passive reporting: subject + is said + perfect passive infinitive (to have been built), because the building happened before the saying.
why.bg: Личен страдателен залог: подлог + is said + перфектен страдателен инфинитив (to have been built), защото строежът е преди говоренето.

questions.first: Lucy finds it very easy to make friends wherever she goes.

why.en: 'Have no difficulty (in) + -ing' = find it easy. 'Has no difficulty to make' is a wrong pattern.
why.bg: 'Have no difficulty (in) + -ing' = не ми е трудно. 'Has no difficulty to make' е грешен модел.

questions.first: Someone stole Mark's wallet while he was on holiday.

why.en: 'Have something + past participle' also describes something bad that happens to you. Word order matters: 'had stolen his wallet' means he stole it.
why.bg: 'Have something + минало причастие' описва и нещо лошо, което ти се случва. Словоредът е важен: 'had stolen his wallet' значи, че той го е откраднал.

questions.first: I'd prefer you not to mention this to anyone.

why.en: 'Would rather + subject + past simple' for a preference about someone else's action. 'I'd rather you not mention' or 'don't mention' lose a mark.
why.bg: 'Would rather + подлог + минало просто време' – предпочитание за действие на друг човек. 'I'd rather you not mention' или 'don't mention' губят точка.

questions.first: She assumed without question that she would get the promotion.

why.en: 'Take it for granted that' = assume something is true without thinking. The 'it' is essential before a that-clause.
why.bg: 'Take it for granted that' = приемам нещо за даденост. 'It' е задължително пред that-изречението.

tests.en: Part 1 is a text with 8 gaps and four options per gap (questions 1–8, 1 mark each). It tests precise vocabulary: collocations, fixed phrases, idioms, phrasal verbs, near-synonyms and what grammar a word needs after it (e.g. 'cope with', 'regardless of').
tests.bg: Част 1 е текст с 8 празни места и по четири варианта за всяко (въпроси 1–8, по 1 точка). Проверява точна лексика: колокации, устойчиви изрази, идиоми, фразови глаголи, близки синоними и каква граматика иска думата след себе си (напр. 'cope with', 'regardless of').

strategy.en: Read the whole text first for gist, without looking at the options.
strategy.bg: Първо прочети целия текст за общия смисъл, без да гледаш вариантите.

strategy.en: For each gap, look at the words on BOTH sides – a preposition or object after the gap often decides the answer.
strategy.bg: За всяко място гледай думите и от двете страни – предлог или допълнение след празното място често решава отговора.

strategy.en: Eliminate options that don't collocate or don't fit the grammar, even if their meaning is close.
strategy.bg: Елиминирай вариантите, които не се съчетават или не пасват граматически, дори смисълът им да е близък.

strategy.en: Read the sentence again with your choice to check it sounds natural.
strategy.bg: Прочети изречението отново с избрания вариант и провери дали звучи естествено.

example.question: The committee was quick to point out that the minister's argument simply didn't ___ water.  A hold  B keep  C carry  D contain

steps.en: All four verbs can go with 'water' in a literal sense (a bucket can hold, keep, carry or contain water), so literal meaning won't decide.
steps.bg: И четирите глагола могат да вървят с 'water' в буквален смисъл (кофа може да hold, keep, carry или contain вода), така че буквалното значение не решава.

steps.en: The subject is an argument, so this must be an idiom. 'Hold water' = be logical and convincing when examined.
steps.bg: Подлогът е аргумент, значи е идиом. 'Hold water' = издържа на проверка, логично е.

steps.en: 'Carry weight' is a similar idiom about arguments, which makes C tempting – but it needs 'weight', not 'water'. The answer is A.
steps.bg: 'Carry weight' е подобен идиом за аргументи и затова C изкушава – но той иска 'weight', не 'water'. Отговорът е A.

pitfalls.en: Choosing a word because it 'means the right thing' without checking the collocation.
pitfalls.bg: Да избереш дума, защото 'значи правилното', без да провериш колокацията.

pitfalls.en: Ignoring the preposition after the gap (e.g. 'aware of', 'attach … to').
pitfalls.bg: Да пренебрегнеш предлога след празното място (напр. 'aware of', 'attach … to').

pitfalls.en: Picking a word just because it is in a phrase you half-remember ('lose the point' instead of 'miss the point').
pitfalls.bg: Да избереш дума само защото е от израз, който помниш наполовина ('lose the point' вместо 'miss the point').

tests.en: Part 2 is an open cloze: 8 gaps (questions 9–16), one word each, no options. Most gaps test grammar words – prepositions, articles, pronouns, auxiliaries, linkers, relative pronouns – and fixed phrases such as 'part and parcel' or 'all but'.
tests.bg: Част 2 е отворен тест: 8 празни места (въпроси 9–16), по една дума, без варианти. Повечето места проверяват граматически думи – предлози, членове, местоимения, спомагателни глаголи, съюзи, относителни местоимения – и устойчиви изрази като 'part and parcel' или 'all but'.

strategy.en: Read the whole text first; the meaning of the paragraph often tells you if you need contrast, cause or addition.
strategy.bg: Първо прочети целия текст; смисълът на абзаца често подсказва дали ти трябва контраст, причина или добавяне.

strategy.en: Decide what part of speech is missing: is there a verb without a subject? A noun without a determiner?
strategy.bg: Определи каква част на речта липсва: има ли глагол без подлог? Съществително без определител?

strategy.en: Look for patterns that need a partner word: 'the more … the more', 'not so much … as', 'so … that'.
strategy.bg: Търси конструкции с 'двойка': 'the more … the more', 'not so much … as', 'so … that'.

strategy.en: Check spelling – a misspelt word scores zero – and never write two words.
strategy.bg: Провери правописа – сгрешена дума носи нула точки – и никога не пиши две думи.

example.question: ___ it not for the volunteers, the festival could never take place.

steps.en: There is no 'if' and the verb 'take place' is in a conditional form, so this is probably an inverted conditional.
steps.bg: Няма 'if', а 'could never take place' е условна форма – вероятно е условно изречение с инверсия.

steps.en: 'If it were not for' becomes 'Were it not for' when we drop 'if'. 'Had' would need 'been' after 'not'.
steps.bg: 'If it were not for' става 'Were it not for', когато махнем 'if'. 'Had' би изисквало 'been' след 'not'.

pitfalls.en: Writing contractions or two words (e.g. 'even though') in one gap.
pitfalls.bg: Да пишеш съкращения или две думи (напр. 'even though') в едно място.

pitfalls.en: Choosing a word that fits the sentence but not the paragraph (e.g. 'and' where the text needs contrast).
pitfalls.bg: Да избереш дума, която пасва на изречението, но не и на абзаца (напр. 'and', когато текстът иска контраст).

pitfalls.en: Forgetting agreement: 'its' vs 'their', 'much' vs 'many'.
pitfalls.bg: Да забравиш съгласуването: 'its' или 'their', 'much' или 'many'.

tests.en: Part 3 is word formation: 8 gaps (questions 17–24). You change the word in capitals so it fits the gap. At C1 you often need more than one change – a prefix and a suffix (unwillingness), an internal change (ingenious → ingenuity), a plural, or a compound (long-term).
tests.bg: Част 3 е словообразуване: 8 празни места (въпроси 17–24). Променяш думата с главни букви, за да пасне. На ниво C1 често трябват няколко промени – представка и наставка (unwillingness), вътрешна промяна (ingenious → ingenuity), множествено число или сложна дума (long-term).

strategy.en: Decide the part of speech the gap needs: after an article → noun; before a noun → adjective; modifying an adjective or verb → adverb.
strategy.bg: Определи каква част на речта трябва: след член → съществително; пред съществително → прилагателно; към прилагателно или глагол → наречие.

strategy.en: Read the whole sentence to decide if the meaning is positive or negative – many C1 answers need a negative prefix.
strategy.bg: Прочети цялото изречение, за да прецениш дали смисълът е положителен или отрицателен – много отговори на C1 искат отрицателна представка.

strategy.en: Check singular or plural: look at the verb and determiners around the gap.
strategy.bg: Провери единствено или множествено число: виж глагола и определителите около празното място.

strategy.en: Spell carefully – answers with spelling mistakes get no marks.
strategy.bg: Пиши внимателно – отговор с правописна грешка не носи точка.

example.question: Critics dismissed the report as ___ (ALARM), saying the risks were greatly exaggerated.

steps.en: After 'dismissed … as' we need an adjective or noun describing the report.
steps.bg: След 'dismissed … as' трябва прилагателно или съществително, което описва доклада.

steps.en: 'Alarming' (worrying) is a real adjective, but the second half says the risks were exaggerated – so the critics think the report spreads unnecessary fear.
steps.bg: 'Alarming' (тревожен) съществува, но втората част казва, че рисковете са преувеличени – значи критиците смятат, че докладът всява излишна паника.

pitfalls.en: Forming a real word that doesn't fit the meaning (imaginary instead of imaginative).
pitfalls.bg: Да образуваш съществуваща дума, която не пасва по смисъл (imaginary вместо imaginative).

pitfalls.en: Forgetting a negative prefix or plural -s – one missing letter loses the mark.
pitfalls.bg: Да забравиш отрицателна представка или -s за множествено число – една липсваща буква губи точката.

pitfalls.en: Using the wrong negative prefix (unpossible, inevitable as 'unevitable').
pitfalls.bg: Да сложиш грешна отрицателна представка (unpossible, 'unevitable').

tests.en: Part 4 is key word transformation: 6 sentences (questions 25–30, 2 marks each). You complete a second sentence with 3–6 words, including the key word unchanged, so that it means the same as the first. It tests grammar (inversion, passives, conditionals, wish, cleft sentences) and vocabulary (idioms, collocations, phrasal verbs).
tests.bg: Част 4 е трансформация с ключова дума: 6 изречения (въпроси 25–30, по 2 точки). Довършваш второ изречение с 3–6 думи, включително ключовата дума без промяна, така че да значи същото като първото. Проверява граматика (инверсия, пасив, условни, wish, цепени изречения) и лексика (идиоми, колокации, фразови глаголи).

strategy.en: Identify what the key word forces: 'LITTLE' at the start suggests inversion, 'SAID' a passive reporting verb, 'WISH' a past tense.
strategy.bg: Разбери какво налага ключовата дума: 'LITTLE' в началото подсказва инверсия, 'SAID' – безличен пасив, 'WISH' – минало време.

strategy.en: Look at the words before and after the gap – they fix the grammar of your answer.
strategy.bg: Виж думите преди и след празното място – те определят граматиката на отговора.

strategy.en: Check that every piece of meaning from the first sentence is still there (time, negative, who did what).
strategy.bg: Провери дали целият смисъл от първото изречение е запазен (време, отрицание, кой какво е направил).

strategy.en: Count your words: contractions count as two (didn't = did not).
strategy.bg: Преброй думите: съкращенията се броят за две (didn't = did not).

example.question: People believe that the fire was started deliberately. BELIEVED → The fire ___ started deliberately.

steps.en: 'BELIEVED' with 'The fire' as subject = personal passive: subject + is believed + to-infinitive.
steps.bg: 'BELIEVED' с подлог 'The fire' = личен пасив: подлог + is believed + инфинитив с 'to'.

steps.en: The believing is now (present), but the fire happened before, so we need a perfect infinitive: to have been (started).
steps.bg: Мнението е сега, а пожарът е бил по-рано, затова трябва перфектен инфинитив: to have been (started).

steps.en: Count: is / believed / to / have / been = 5 words. One mark for 'is believed', one for 'to have been'.
steps.bg: Брой: is / believed / to / have / been = 5 думи. Една точка за 'is believed', една за 'to have been'.

pitfalls.en: Changing the key word (believe instead of BELIEVED) – this scores zero.
pitfalls.bg: Да промениш ключовата дума (believe вместо BELIEVED) – носи нула точки.

pitfalls.en: Writing more than six words or leaving out part of the meaning.
pitfalls.bg: Да напишеш повече от шест думи или да изпуснеш част от смисъла.

pitfalls.en: Forgetting inversion after negative openers ('Little the minister knew').
pitfalls.bg: Да забравиш инверсията след отрицателни начала ('Little the minister knew').

tests.en: Part 5 is one long text (650–800 words) with 6 four-option questions (31–36, 2 marks each). It tests detail, the writer's opinion and attitude, purpose, tone, implication and the meaning of words or phrases in context. Questions follow the order of the text.
tests.bg: Част 5 е един дълъг текст (650–800 думи) с 6 въпроса с по четири варианта (31–36, по 2 точки). Проверява детайли, мнението и отношението на автора, цел, тон, подразбиране и значението на думи и изрази в контекст. Въпросите следват реда на текста.

strategy.en: Skim the text first for the writer's overall argument and attitude.
strategy.bg: Първо прегледай текста бързо, за да хванеш основната теза и отношението на автора.

strategy.en: Read each question stem (not the options) and find the part of the text it refers to.
strategy.bg: Прочети въпроса (без вариантите) и намери частта от текста, за която се отнася.

strategy.en: Decide what the text says in your own words, then choose the option that matches that meaning.
strategy.bg: Формулирай със свои думи какво казва текстът, после избери варианта, който съвпада по смисъл.

strategy.en: Check why each of the other options is wrong: not stated, the opposite, or true but not the answer to this question.
strategy.bg: Провери защо всеки от другите варианти е грешен: не се казва, обратното е, или е вярно, но не отговаря на въпроса.

example.question: Text: 'I used to bristle at this question. Now I find it rather useful.' — How does the writer now feel about the question?  A irritated  B grateful for the opportunity it gives

steps.en: 'Used to bristle' describes the past, so irritation is no longer true – a classic trap.
steps.bg: 'Used to bristle' описва миналото, така че раздразнението вече не е вярно – класически капан.

steps.en: 'Now I find it rather useful' matches B, which paraphrases 'useful' without repeating the word.
steps.bg: 'Now I find it rather useful' съвпада с B, което перифразира 'useful', без да повтаря думата.

example.answer: B grateful for the opportunity it gives

pitfalls.en: Choosing an option because it repeats words from the text – the right answer is usually a paraphrase.
pitfalls.bg: Да избереш вариант, защото повтаря думи от текста – верният отговор обикновено е перифраза.

pitfalls.en: Answering from general knowledge instead of what the writer actually says.
pitfalls.bg: Да отговориш по обща култура вместо според това, което авторът казва.

pitfalls.en: Missing time signals (used to, now, at first) that change the writer's attitude.
pitfalls.bg: Да пропуснеш сигнали за време (used to, now, at first), които променят отношението на автора.

tests.en: Part 6 has four short texts (A–D) by different writers on the same topic and 4 questions (37–40, 2 marks each). You compare opinions across the texts: which writer shares or contradicts another writer's view on a particular point.
tests.bg: Част 6 има четири кратки текста (A–D) от различни автори по една тема и 4 въпроса (37–40, по 2 точки). Сравняваш мненията между текстовете: кой автор споделя или оспорва мнението на друг по конкретен въпрос.

strategy.en: Read the questions first and note the topics they mention (e.g. cost, residents' attitudes, evidence).
strategy.bg: Първо прочети въпросите и отбележи темите в тях (напр. разходи, отношение на жителите, доказателства).

strategy.en: Make a small grid: for each topic, mark each writer's view (+, −, or not mentioned).
strategy.bg: Направи малка таблица: за всяка тема отбележи мнението на всеки автор (+, − или не се споменава).

strategy.en: For 'different from the others' questions, look for the one writer who disagrees with the other three.
strategy.bg: При въпроси 'различно от останалите' търси единствения автор, който не е съгласен с другите трима.

strategy.en: For 'shares A's view' questions, find A's view first, then check B, C and D.
strategy.bg: При въпроси 'споделя мнението на A' първо намери мнението на A, после провери B, C и D.

example.question: A: 'Opposition melted away once the flowers bloomed.' C: 'Hostility did not fade; if anything, it hardened.' D: 'The outcry rarely lasts.' — Which writer has a different view about how residents' attitudes change?

steps.en: A and D both say residents come round over time.
steps.bg: A и D казват, че жителите свикват с времето.

steps.en: C says hostility grew stronger, so C is the odd one out.
steps.bg: C казва, че враждебността се засилва, значи C е различният.

pitfalls.en: Choosing a writer who mentions the topic but expresses no clear opinion on it.
pitfalls.bg: Да избереш автор, който споменава темата, но не изразява ясно мнение.

pitfalls.en: Matching words rather than views – two writers may use the same word with opposite meanings.
pitfalls.bg: Да търсиш еднакви думи вместо еднакви мнения – двама автори може да използват една дума с противоположен смисъл.

pitfalls.en: Not noticing concessions ('That said…', 'I would caution, however…') that change a writer's position.
pitfalls.bg: Да не забележиш отстъпки ('That said…', 'I would caution, however…'), които променят позицията на автора.

tests.en: Part 7 is a long text with six paragraphs removed (questions 41–46, 2 marks each). You choose the right paragraph for each gap from seven options (A–G); one is extra. It tests how texts hang together: reference words, linkers, time order and the development of ideas.
tests.bg: Част 7 е дълъг текст, от който са махнати шест абзаца (въпроси 41–46, по 2 точки). Избираш правилния абзац за всяко място от седем варианта (A–G); един е излишен. Проверява как текстът се свързва: думи за препратка, съюзи, хронология и развитие на идеите.

strategy.en: Read the main text first to understand the overall structure and the story or argument.
strategy.bg: Първо прочети основния текст, за да разбереш структурата и историята или аргумента.

strategy.en: For each gap, read the paragraph before AND after it – the missing paragraph must link to both.
strategy.bg: За всяко място прочети абзаца преди И след него – липсващият абзац трябва да се свързва и с двата.

strategy.en: Look for reference clues in the options: 'This', 'such', 'that story', names, 'But', 'Yet'.
strategy.bg: Търси думи за препратка във вариантите: 'This', 'such', 'that story', имена, 'But', 'Yet'.

strategy.en: Do the easiest gaps first, then check the remaining options carefully against the remaining gaps.
strategy.bg: Започни от най-лесните места, после внимателно сравни останалите варианти с останалите места.

example.question: Before the gap: '…on one memorable occasion, the car park of a supermarket.' After the gap: 'Identifying a variety is painstaking work.' Option: 'That story, which he clearly enjoys telling, involved a single gnarled tree…'

steps.en: 'That story' needs something to refer back to – 'one memorable occasion' in the car park is exactly that.
steps.bg: 'That story' има нужда от нещо, към което да препраща – 'one memorable occasion' на паркинга е точно това.

steps.en: The option finishes the anecdote, so the next paragraph can move on to a new topic (identification).
steps.bg: Вариантът приключва историята, така че следващият абзац може да мине към нова тема (идентифицирането).

example.answer: That story, which he clearly enjoys telling…

pitfalls.en: Checking only the paragraph before the gap and ignoring the one after.
pitfalls.bg: Да провериш само абзаца преди мястото и да пренебрегнеш този след него.

pitfalls.en: Choosing a paragraph because it is on the same topic, without a real linguistic link.
pitfalls.bg: Да избереш абзац, защото е по същата тема, без реална езикова връзка.

pitfalls.en: Forgetting that one option is extra – if an option seems to fit nowhere, it may be the distractor.
pitfalls.bg: Да забравиш, че един вариант е излишен – ако някой не пасва никъде, може да е той.

tests.en: Part 8 is one long text in sections or several short texts (A–D/E/F) with 10 statements (questions 47–56, 1 mark each). You decide which section each statement refers to. It tests finding specific information, detail, opinion and implication quickly.
tests.bg: Част 8 е един дълъг текст на секции или няколко кратки текста (A–D/E/F) с 10 твърдения (въпроси 47–56, по 1 точка). Решаваш за коя секция се отнася всяко твърдение. Проверява бързо намиране на конкретна информация, детайли, мнения и подразбиране.

strategy.en: Read the statements first and underline the key idea in each (e.g. 'regrets', 'surprised their family').
strategy.bg: Първо прочети твърденията и подчертай ключовата идея във всяко (напр. 'regrets', 'surprised their family').

strategy.en: Read each section and note which statements it might match.
strategy.bg: Прочети всяка секция и отбележи кои твърдения може да пасват.

strategy.en: Expect paraphrase: 'a disaster at school' = 'performed poorly as a student'.
strategy.bg: Очаквай перифраза: 'a disaster at school' = 'performed poorly as a student'.

strategy.en: When two sections seem to match, reread the statement for the exact detail (who, when, positive or negative).
strategy.bg: Ако две секции изглеждат подходящи, препрочети твърдението за точния детайл (кой, кога, положително или отрицателно).

example.question: Statement: 'credits a particular teacher with influencing their decision'. A: 'My biology teacher was kind but rather uninspiring.' C: 'Mrs Okonjo … persuaded me to apply for a science degree.'

steps.en: Both A and C mention a teacher, so the word 'teacher' alone isn't enough.
steps.bg: И A, и C споменават учител, така че самата дума 'teacher' не стига.

steps.en: The statement needs the teacher to have influenced the decision. Only C says the teacher persuaded her.
steps.bg: Твърдението изисква учителят да е повлиял на решението. Само C казва, че учителката я е убедила.

pitfalls.en: Matching a section because it contains the same word as the statement.
pitfalls.bg: Да свържеш секция, защото съдържа същата дума като твърдението.

pitfalls.en: Spending too long on one statement – move on and come back.
pitfalls.bg: Да се бавиш твърде дълго на едно твърдение – продължи и се върни после.

pitfalls.en: Missing negatives or opposites (e.g. a parent who 'took it for granted' vs a family that was surprised).
pitfalls.bg: Да пропуснеш отрицания или противоположности (напр. родител, който 'took it for granted', срещу изненадано семейство).
